root_cause.text: The vulnerability exists because the `nf_hook_ops` structures in the netfilter NAT subsystem are freed immediately with `kfree` instead of using RCU-based deferred reclamation, causing potential use-after-free when accessed concurrently by the userspace hook dump feature introduced in v5.14.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that v5.14 added the ability to "dump the active netfilter hooks from userspace" which "will peek back into the nf_hook_ops," necessitating that "the nat ops structures have to be deferred too," and the patch diff confirms this by replacing `kfree(ops)` and `kfree(nat_ops)` with `kfree_rcu(ops, rcu)` and `kfree_rcu(nat_ops, rcu)` in `nf_nat_register_fn`, `nf_nat_unregister_fn`, and related lookup functions.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The netfilter NAT subsystem improperly freed `nf_hook_ops` structures using synchronous `kfree()` calls instead of RCU-deferred `kfree_rcu()`, allowing use-after-free when the v5.14 userspace hook dumping feature accessed these structures.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch replaces `kfree(nat_ops)` and `kfree(ops)` with `kfree_rcu(nat_ops, rcu)` and `kfree_rcu(ops, rcu)` in `nf_nat_core.c` and NAT initialization files, consistent with the CVE description stating that the v5.14 userspace hook dumping feature exposes `nf_hook_ops` which must now be deferred to prevent accessing freed memory.
